title: Inspect shared commander and command instruments
description: The developer gallery renders the actual CommanderDeck, CommanderPortrait, CommandControl and GameMenu. Its existing reducer-derived scenario is explicitly a component demonstration, not an authenticated campaign, admission or privacy claim. Keyboard and local preview outcomes are named separately from service acknowledgements.

steps.description: Read the actual commander deck, open its portrait menu with Enter, and traverse every modal control including both wrap boundaries.
steps.acknowledgement: The actual native game menu contains focus at its final control.
verifications: This is the browser-local presentation menu, not campaign navigation or a fabricated order.

steps.description: Escape restores the exact portrait opener. Read the own and peer controls; compact phone uses the own portrait while live Roster remains covered by the campaign story.
steps.acknowledgement: The commander opener regains focus and the modal closes.
verifications: Responsive peer visibility and semantic cosmetic/faction labelling are retained.

steps.description: Activate a peer portrait through Space and observe the gallery callback acknowledgement, explicitly not a server receipt.
steps.acknowledgement: The actual deck delivers its roster callback.
verifications: The initiating peer control retains keyboard focus in this component demonstration.

steps.description: Read all six shared command instruments and the disabled example, then select History with the keyboard.
steps.acknowledgement: The local preview names History and exposes its current state to assistive technology.
verifications: All real icon controls remain labelled; only one is current and the explicit disabled example cannot be activated.

steps.description: Read all eight cosmetic portrait tiles from the original approved atlas, rendered by the shared production portrait component.
steps.acknowledgement: Eight labelled atlas tiles are rendered from the production portrait asset.
verifications: The atlas uses the existing provenanced image and every tile has a contained readable caption.
